competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sample items directly fulfill the competency requirement of determining next terms in patterns. Items successfully assess increasing number patterns such as "What is the next number in the pattern: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12?", decreasing number patterns such as "What is the next number in the pattern: 30, 28, 26, 24, 22, 20?" and "What is the next number in the pattern: 15, 13, 11, 9, 7, 5?", repeating letter sequences like "What is the next letter in the pattern: e, d, e, d, e, d?", and visual pattern identification in "What is the missing piece (position 6) in the pattern?".

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The items cover the full breadth of the MATATAG specification including increasing numbers ("What is the next number in the pattern: 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22?"), decreasing numbers ("What is the next number in the pattern: 20, 19, 18, 17, 16, 15?"), alternating and 3-element letter sequences ("What is the next letter in the pattern: f, o, c, f, o, c?"), repeating multi-digit numbers ("What is the next number in the pattern: 68, 81, 76, 68, 81, 76?"), and visual elements ("What is the missing piece (position 6) in the pattern?").

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The cognitive demands are well-calibrated for Grade 2 Quarter 2 students. Pattern steps are straightforward (e.g., skip counting by 2s or decrements by 1) and question stems are clear and concise without extraneous reading load, as seen in "What is the next number in the pattern: 20, 19, 18, 17, 16, 15?" and "What is the next letter in the pattern: e, d, e, d, e, d?".

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The sample set provides healthy format and variant diversity, utilizing multiple-choice format (mcq) in "What is the next number in the pattern: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12?", cloze completion in "What is the next number in the pattern: 68, 81, 76, 68, 81, 76?", and visual reading comprehension (read_mcq) in "What is the missing piece (position 6) in the pattern?".

competency_alignment.rationale: Every question is strictly aligned with the target learning competency, focusing entirely on pattern recognition and sequence extension without drifting into unrelated arithmetic operations or out-of-grade algebraic notation. For instance, "What is the next letter in the pattern: f, o, c, f, o, c?" and "What is the next number in the pattern: 15, 13, 11, 9, 7, 5?" focus purely on next-term determination.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The numerical magnitudes and step sizes are appropriate for Grade 2. Sequence ranges stay within accessible bounds (under 100), using single-step intervals in "What is the next number in the pattern: 20, 19, 18, 17, 16, 15?", standard skip counting in "What is the next number in the pattern: 30, 28, 26, 24, 22, 20?", and 6-term sequence lengths that give enough context to identify the core unit without overwhelming young learners.
